temptingClaims: Einstein's 1905 argument about simultaneity uses lightning striking the two ends of a moving train.
whyTempting: The picture of lightning at the ends of a train and an embankment is the most familiar illustration of the relativity of simultaneity.
whereItIsTrue: The paper does argue that simultaneity depends on the system from which it is judged, and it does so with light signals between two places.

whatIsTrue.r0: The paper's argument uses clocks at two places, A and B, and a light signal sent from A, reflected at B and returned. There is no train and no lightning in it.
whatIsTrue.r1: § 1 defines a common time for two places: a ray of light leaves A at the A-time \(t_A\), is reflected at B at the B-time \(t_B\), and arrives back at A at \(t'_A\); the two clocks run synchronously by definition if \(t_B - t_A = t'_A - t_B\) (pp. 893–894). § 2 applies the rule to a moving rod with clocks at its ends, and shows that clocks synchronous in the stationary system are not synchronous for observers moving with the rod (pp. 895–897). SR-01 runs the rule: with stations 5 light-seconds apart and emission at 0, the reflection is assigned the time 5.
whatIsTrue.r2: (1) § 1: clocks at A and B, identical, each giving the time of events near it. (2) The definition: send light from A to B and back, and set B's clock so that the time out equals the time back, \(t_B - t_A = t'_A - t_B\) (p. 894). (3) With emission at 0 and return at 10, the reflection is at 5. (4) § 2: a rod moving along the line, with clocks at its ends synchronous in the stationary system; observers moving with the rod, applying the same rule, find them not synchronous (pp. 896–897). (5) So the paper's instruments are clocks and light signals between two places, not a train and lightning.
whatIsTrue.r3: The train-and-embankment picture is a later popular illustration of §§ 1–2. This entry does not cite where it appeared, because the site's bibliography holds no checked record of it.

sources: A. Einstein, Ann. Phys. (4) 17, 891–921 (1905), plates pp. 893–897
